# The follow-up call list nobody owns

Every week a list of patients due for a follow-up call gets printed from the appointment system. The question of whose job it is to actually make those calls has never been formally assigned, which means in practice it gets done by whoever has a free half hour and remembers the list exists, most weeks the same one nurse, some weeks nobody.

The list itself is not even reliably accurate; it is generated from the original referral date rather than from whatever the actual first-visit outcome was, so it includes some patients who were already discharged from the follow-up requirement at visit one and were never removed. Staff who have tried to use the list say roughly a fifth of the names on it turn out not to need a call at all, which erodes confidence in the other four-fifths and makes the whole list feel like more trouble than it is worth to work through carefully every week.
